notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text begins with the title Unconscious Processes Improve Lie Detection, citation to Reinhard, Greifeneder, and Scharmach (2013), JPSP 105, 721–739, DOI 10.1037/a0034352, and matching author byline. It contains the primary manuscript with experiment methods/results, references, tables, and figure captions, rather than an abstract-only parse or secondary account. Manuscript pagination differs from journal pagination. No PDF was supplied. The description identifies discrimination ability; the reported partial eta squared is for the omnibus thinking-mode effect on d′. Separate planned contrasts on manuscript p. 15 report unconscious vs standard control F(1, 60) = 5.40, p = .023, d = 0.69, and unconscious vs conscious thought F(1, 60) = 4.28, p = .043, d = 0.60; these are separate tests, not combined with the omnibus statistics. Criterion C is response bias and not the requested discrimination outcome. No metric conversion performed. Only es_value_o and pval_value_o were assigned; N, replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders, not findings of absence.
